q: Fill up: First-trimester dating uses the ______, which is accurate to within ______ days.
exp: The crown-rump length dates pregnancy to within 5-7 days, far better than second-trimester biparietal diameter.

sec: Second trimester biometry, cervical length & fetal echo
q: A 29-year-old primigravida with no prior preterm birth has a transvaginal cervical length of 20 mm at 22 weeks and no contractions. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Start vaginal micronised progesterone 200 mg nightly and repeat the cervical length
Perform an immediate McDonald cerclage, because 20 mm is an absolute operative indication
Advise strict bed rest alone, since no intervention has proven benefit
exp: An incidental short cervix of 25 mm or less in a woman without a prior preterm birth is treated with vaginal progesterone, not immediate cerclage.

sec: Anomaly scan (TIFFA) & cranial NTDs: anencephaly & acrania
q: Match the cranial defect with its sonographic appearance — 1) Acrania 2) Exencephaly 3) Anencephaly … A) Skull vault absent but formed brain tissue still present B) Disorganised brain tissue floating in amniotic fluid with no skull C) No brain tissue above the orbits, giving the frog-face appearance
exp: Acrania and exencephaly are successive stages of the same process that ends as anencephaly with absent cerebrum.

sec: Spina bifida, Arnold-Chiari II signs & craniorachischisis
q: Fill up: On the axial head view, scalloping of the frontal bones gives the ______ sign and the displaced cerebellum gives the ______ sign of Arnold-Chiari II malformation.
exp: The lemon sign is frontal bone scalloping and the banana sign is the herniated, flattened cerebellum of the Chiari II malformation.

sec: Abdominal wall defects: omphalocele vs gastroschisis
q: All of the following describe omphalocele EXCEPT:
opts: Bowel loops float freely with no covering membrane over them
The umbilical cord inserts into the covering sac
It is a midline defect and often contains the liver
It is strongly associated with chromosomal anomalies and cardiac defects
exp: An uncovered sac is gastroschisis; omphalocele is a midline, membrane-covered defect with the cord on the sac and a high anomaly rate.

q: Which of the following statements about alpha-fetoprotein is TRUE?
opts: Open spina bifida raises amniotic fluid AFP and acetylcholinesterase, while gastroschisis raises AFP alone
A low maternal serum AFP is diagnostic of trisomy 21 and needs no further assessment
Maternal serum AFP interpretation is unaffected by incorrect gestational dating
Amniotic fluid AFP is normally far higher than fetal serum AFP in a closed neural tube defect
exp: Amniotic fluid AFP plus acetylcholinesterase is specific for open defects; wrong dating is the commonest cause of a spurious AFP result.

q: Fill up: About ______% of Down syndrome is caused by meiotic non-disjunction, and the extra chromosome is of ______ origin in the great majority.
exp: Roughly 95% is non-disjunction, mostly maternal and rising with maternal age; the rest is translocation or mosaic.

sec: First trimester screening: dual test & combined test
q: Match the test with what it measures — 1) Dual test 2) First-trimester combined test 3) Quadruple test … A) Nuchal translucency plus beta-hCG and PAPP-A with maternal age B) Beta-hCG and PAPP-A alone C) AFP, beta-hCG, unconjugated estriol and inhibin A
exp: The dual test is biochemical only; adding nuchal translucency makes it the combined test, and the quad test belongs to the second trimester.

q: Which of the following statements about nuchal translucency is TRUE?
opts: With a nuchal translucency above 3.5 mm and a normal karyotype, a fetal echocardiogram and detailed anatomy scan are indicated
Cystic hygroma is a thin, septation-free collection that always resolves by the middle of the second trimester
Nuchal translucency may be measured at any gestational age between 14 and 20 weeks
A nuchal translucency of 2.5 mm is above the 99th centile at every crown-rump length
exp: NT is measured at 11 to 13+6 weeks; a very thick NT with normal chromosomes warrants cardiac and anatomical follow-up, and septated cystic hygroma has a worse prognosis.

sec: Second trimester markers: triple, quad & soft sonographic signs
q: All of the following are soft sonographic markers of trisomy 21 EXCEPT:
exp: Choroid plexus cysts are the classic trisomy 18 marker; nuchal fold thickening, short long bones and echogenic bowel are trisomy 21 markers.

sec: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT / cffDNA) & integrated screening
q: Match the test with what it is — 1) cffDNA or NIPT 2) Chorionic villus sampling 3) Amniocentesis … A) Screening test using placental DNA fragments in maternal blood B) Diagnostic test on placental tissue from 10-13 weeks C) Diagnostic test on amniotic fluid, usually after 15 weeks
exp: NIPT remains a screening test because the DNA is placental; CVS and amniocentesis give a definitive fetal karyotype.

q: A 38-year-old at 12 weeks has a combined-test risk of 1 in 80 for trisomy 21. She wants certainty but is frightened of procedure-related loss. What is the correct counselling?
opts: Offer diagnostic testing by CVS or amniocentesis, because NIPT remains a screening test at this risk
Reassure her that 1 in 80 is screen-negative and no further testing is needed
Offer NIPT and terminate the pregnancy if it is high risk, without confirmatory testing
Repeat the combined test at 16 weeks to obtain a definitive result
exp: A screen-positive result must be confirmed by a diagnostic test before any irreversible decision, and screening tests cannot be repeated as if they were diagnostic.
